item.title: The Swannanoa Gathering Public Concerts — Tue Jul 28, 7:30 PM — Warren Wilson College Swannanoa
item.description:
The Swannanoa Gathering was established in 1992 as a vision of Warren Wilson College President Doug Orr and founding Director Jim Magill to host summer workshops celebrating the music and dance traditions of the southern Appalachian region and beyond.
Big news…Our staff concerts will now be open to the public!
We’re excited to be able to share our incredibly talented staff with Asheville and the surrounding Western North Carolina community. Tickets will be available for purchase online and at the door.
The Swannanoa Gathering is an educational program of the college, consisting of a series of week-long workshops in various folk arts held on the campus of Warren Wilson College just east of Asheville in the heart of North Carolina’s beautiful Blue Ridge Mountains. Tickets are $35 per concert. Event Details & Tickets https://swangathering.com/about-us/public-concerts/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Jul 29 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

Make a visible difference on the French Broad River while spending the day alongside other young professionals who care about Asheville and Western North Carolina.
AYPROS is sponsoring a hands-on river cleanup with Asheville GreenWorks on Saturday, August 1. Volunteers will paddle canoes, with some participants potentially using kayaks, along a section of the French Broad River. We will stop frequently to remove litter from the water, riverbanks, and surrounding muddy areas.
This is not a simple walk along the shoreline. Volunteers should expect to enter water that may reach or rise above their waists, move through muddy spaces, and get dirty. item.title: Dealing with Difficult Emotions — Sun Aug 2, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism Dealing with Difficult Emotions with Modern Buddhism Teacher Jill Cagney
**Sundays 6/28-8/9 10:30am-11:45am** Overwhelmed by your feelings? Buddhist psychology offers a time-tested, powerful and healthy approach to dealing with painful, challenging emotions. Each week, we will apply these methods to states like craving, anger, jealousy, and self-hatred. First, we need to recognize them, learn how they work, and accept ourselves for where we are, Next, we can disempower them using special meditations. Finally, we can envision and even experience a state of total freedom and release, having transcended these difficult emotions. Cost: $12 (free and online options for members) [Read More and Register](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/sunday-drop-in-meditation-class/) [Become a Member](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/become-a-member/)

item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

item.title: The Shape of Repair: Patchwork in Wood Exhibition — Thu Aug 20, 12:00 AM
item.description:
The S. Tucker Cooke Gallery presents an exhibition of work by sculptor Laura Petrovich-Cheney. Using salvaged architectural wood, Petrovich-Cheney creates quilt-inspired wall pieces that explore memory, repair, and renewal. Her geometric compositions draw on the visual language of patchwork while transforming discarded materials into contemporary works of art. The exhibition is on view August 20 through September 11 and is free and open to the public.
